evaluations.evidence: entering a name and an optional description
evaluations.rationale: Specifies the data/need for creating a game but does not prescribe UI widgets or implementation mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: giving them a URL where they can access the game
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a concrete invitation mechanism (URL) rather than stating the stakeholder need to invite estimators.

evaluations.evidence: entering an item in a single multi-line text field
evaluations.rationale: Explicitly prescribes a specific UI widget (single multi-line text field).

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: States the stakeholder need without prescribing implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Describes required functionality without specifying UI widgets or technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Functional need expressed; no unnecessary implementation choices.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Describes editing capability but does not prescribe how to implement it.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Functional requirement without implementation detail.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: States behavior/need but does not prescribe UI widgets or technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific algorithm/decision rule (average) rather than the stakeholder need generally.

evaluations.evidence: "estimate" field filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Describes desired automatic behavior; mentions a field but does not mandate a concrete UI widget or technical mechanism.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Functional need to record the agreed estimate without implementation constraints.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Describes capability required, not a specific implementation.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a concrete data source/format (spreadsheet) as the mechanism for importing, an implementation detail.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific mechanism and data format (copy/paste from spreadsheet).

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: User need stated without implementation detail.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: Functional requirement without prescribing how to implement it.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a concrete export file format (HTML), which is an implementation choice.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific export format (CSV), a technical implementation detail.

evaluations.evidence: delete a game, so that stories and estimates for this game are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: Expresses the need to remove stored data but does not prescribe how to implement deletion.

evaluations.evidence: entering my name, email address, a password and a username
evaluations.rationale: Specifies account data to collect (user need) but does not mandate specific UI widgets or backend mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Describes the authentication credential type desired; not an implementation technology or internal mechanism.

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: High-level user need without implementation constraints.

evaluations.evidence: delete my account, so that account information and games are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: Functional need to remove account and related data; not prescribing internal mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: User-observable requirement; does not prescribe a specific implementation.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a concrete delivery mechanism (email) for password reminders, which is an implementation choice.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Defines domain-specific option sets for estimation values; this expresses stakeholder preference rather than low-level technical implementation.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a capacity/limit requirement, not a technical mechanism or UI widget.

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Refers to joining via a URL-delivered page (a specific access mechanism), which prescribes the invite/access method.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: Clear stakeholder need without prescribing implementation.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Functional need; no implementation details specified.

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: Describes desired visibility of actions, not how to implement that visibility.

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Functional requirement about timing of display without prescribing mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: be able to change my estimate up until the last person selects a card and all are shown
evaluations.rationale: Specifies allowed user behavior and termination condition; not an implementation detail.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Describes information the user needs without prescribing technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: User-visible requirement, not an implementation choice.

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: Specifies desired behavior and duration but does not prescribe UI widget or technical mechanism.

evaluations.evidence: two-minute timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Behavioral requirement describing when the timer resets; not a concrete implementation choice.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: User capability requirement without prescribing implementation.

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Specifies consistent UX behavior but does not mandate internal implementation.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: Describes permitted user action and condition; not an implementation detail.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific UI element and its placement (thumbnail near cards), which is a UI design choice.

evaluations.evidence: compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Specifies particular web standards as an implementation/technical requirement rather than a stakeholder need.

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: Expresses need for shared definitions; not an implementation detail.

evaluations.evidence: have created database indexes
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes an implementation-level optimization (database indexes) rather than a stakeholder-level need.

evaluations.evidence: function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Specifies concrete platform/browser support (implementation constraint) rather than the stakeholder need in general.

evaluations.evidence: comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines where possible
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes adherence to a specific standard/guideline (an implementation constraint).

evaluations.evidence: have the application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: Describes a non-functional user need (performance) without prescribing how to achieve it.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a concrete encoding/format requirement (Unicode), which is a technical implementation choice.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: Expresses a user-facing expectation about URL readability/behavior rather than prescribing internal implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: User-oriented quality need; does not mandate technical implementation.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: Expresses a privacy requirement (non-identifiable storage) as a stakeholder need; it does not prescribe a specific storage technology or format.

evaluations.evidence: see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: Describes a user need for metrics without prescribing how metrics are collected or implemented.
